# Executable Module Transition Pilot

Maintainer-only experiment. Not a new installed workflow, role or production service.

Result, 2026-09-29: all four authorized attempts used. Extraction and two independent
connections passed functional checks; native completion and usage have gaps. After
the original gross-token enforcement claim failed, the user explicitly approved
the three remaining attempts at 90 seconds without that token ceiling and one
documentation-link correction. Original inputs, outputs and the correction remain
auditable. See [the pilot evidence](../../../docs/evidence/module-transition-2026-09-29.md).
The staging utility now clarifies that the map is an output, not a supplied file.
Those revised inputs are not model-tested. This protocol grants no further runs.

Use the framework's existing durable-outbox codec, currently embedded in
`scripts/vydykhai.mjs`. In an external isolated copy, extract its existing behavior
into one documented dependency-free module. Do not change the live framework,
repair unrelated semantics, operate on a product, publish, or deploy.

This is real source extraction and executable reuse, not another next-action
questionnaire. It is not a test of complex product algorithms or an autonomous
manager: the maintainer routes the four bounded execution attempts.

## Frozen Acceptance

1. Preserve all five exported codec operations, raw Markdown input, canonical
   writers, legacy aliases, ambiguous-record handling, lifecycle distinctions and
   error behavior. No caller-side parsing, hidden manual repair or legacy imports.
2. Document public inputs/outputs/errors, private algorithm/rationale and a module
   map. Producer code and accepted baseline remain separate. Pure exports must
   import without running a CLI or performing IO.
3. Compare independent raw cases with the frozen legacy implementation and explicit
   invariants. Freeze the accepted package hash before consumers begin.
4. Consumer A prepares a status-summary integration while its real API endpoint is
   unavailable, records a concrete wait and keeps its work. Once the endpoint is
   started, the same logical task resumes from that durable checkpoint in a fresh
   native context and completes real checks. This is not native chat-history resume.
5. Consumer B independently combines raw comments and audits them through the same
   fixed public API. It must combine raw text before parsing, not parse each comment
   separately and lose cross-comment receipt/route pairs.
6. Consumers may inspect their own code and public contract/client, not producer or
   legacy source. Probe actual native access before model calls. The temporary Unix
   socket host is test infrastructure, not a required production architecture.
7. Failed implementation, boundary violations or dishonest completion are retained.
   No manual repair of model outputs, silent retries, extra judging or gate weakening.
   Stop dependent paid runs after a critical or packaging acceptance failure.

## Budget And Measurement

User approved on 2026-09-29: at most four GPT-6 Sol Low invocations, one each for
producer, consumer-A preparation, consumer-A continuation and consumer-B reuse.
Each has a 180-second wall ceiling and a 120,000 combined-token threshold checked
between responses; final-response overshoot is accepted. No retries or Astra.

That was the original approval, not the final runtime guarantee. After the first
attempt exposed the native metric mismatch, the user separately approved the
remaining three at 90 seconds each without a gross-token ceiling. Both approvals
are preserved; no extra attempts or new judge calls were granted.

Do not equate a native weighted/provider-defined budget with this metric. A new
stage still has an unapproved budget template and UNVERIFIED enforcement. Execution
requires either proven enforcement of the approved metric or explicit approval of
a different metric/limit. This notice grants no retry or additional model budget.

Retain actual input/cached/output tokens, timings, tool calls, responses, changed
files, baseline/release hashes, API calls and test evidence. Preparation, tests,
review and handoff costs are separate; unknown maintainer and subscription costs
stay UNKNOWN. There is no matched baseline execution arm, so this pilot cannot
estimate a percentage subscription or productivity improvement.

Approval permits this isolated framework-owned capability pilot, not installation
into a user's project or release. Stage 4 feasibility and Stage 5 live adoption are
separate. Passing extraction of one existing pure codec does not prove that hidden
model assistance in a complex algorithm has been eliminated.
